prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 5 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a landscape 16:9 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same moment's world, painted together: the same people, props, weather, light and colour grade in every panel.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 2 is the reference sheet for phone. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: phone exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one storyboard image with three columns and two rows of equal vertical 9:16 spaces, using five panels in reading order and leaving the bottom-right space blank. Use narrow plain gutters and no lettering, symbols, logos or panel labels. Kasun is a smooth red artist's mannequin and Anudi a smooth blue artist's mannequin, retaining their supplied heights and builds; depict them through poses alone. Render the surroundings and props realistically: rain-wet patched asphalt, concrete pavement, open kerb drainage, weathered commercial buildings, muted green paint, a blue shop awning and warm amber shop illumination. Soft overcast morning light comes from upper camera-left, with subdued colours and gentle wet-ground reflections throughout. The parked three-wheeler has muted dark-green bodywork and a black canopy. Anudi carries an open navy umbrella in her left hand and a structured tan handbag on her right shoulder, its exterior side pocket open. The orange smartphone has a transparent cover and the camera arrangement shown in its reference. It begins in her right hand, appears on the ground in panel three, and is in Kasun's right hand in panels four and five.

Geography: The walking edge runs horizontally from the vending bay at screen left toward the next shopfront at screen right. The three-wheeler is parked beside the kerb at the bay; its rear wheel stands beside the phone's landing patch and an open drain interrupted by rectangular concrete bridging slabs. Behind this starting area are a warm-lit shop beneath a blue awning and an adjoining green-painted wall panel. Farther right, the same pavement continues past a grey shutter and a weathered beige frontage. All cameras remain on the roadward side of the walking line, looking toward the buildings, so both travellers progress across the image toward screen right. The green wall remains on frame left through the change from the retrieval area to the following and encounter positions, becoming more distant as the grey shutter and beige frontage occupy more of the background.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing eye height at the roadward pavement edge, looking across the walking line toward the shopfronts; 28mm wide, full figures, deep focus. Keep the road axis left to right. Background: The three-wheeler anchors frame left, with the blue awning and green-painted wall behind it on the left. Weathered shopfronts extend toward frame right; the kerb and open drain cross the lower frame diagonally toward the right. Kasun's red mannequin stands beside the three-wheeler on the left third, chest and head facing screen right in profile, both hands hanging empty beside his hips. Anudi's blue mannequin is mid-step just to his right, travelling across the frame toward screen right with chest and head aligned along the pavement. Her left hand holds the umbrella shaft, while her right hand holds the orange phone immediately beside the tan handbag's open exterior pocket on her right hip. Keep her full figure, the handset, pocket and wet kerb visible together, with the landing patch still empty.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Low camera at kerb height on the same roadward side, looking slightly upward across the walking edge; 35mm wide with deep focus. Anudi remains side-on and travels toward screen right. Background: The three-wheeler's rear wheel and open drain occupy frame left. The lower green-painted wall remains behind them at upper left, while the narrow pavement and shop bases extend toward frame right. Anudi's blue mannequin occupies the right third in a rightward walking step, chest and head facing screen right in profile. Her left hand grips the umbrella shaft beneath the low open canopy, and her right hand still holds the orange phone beside the handbag pocket on her right hip. Leave a clear patch of wet asphalt between her and the rear wheel at frame left, with the drain and its concrete bridging slab sharply visible.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Standing-height camera on the roadward side, angled down with a 50mm lens into a medium lower-body composition from Kasun's lower chest to the pavement. Prioritise the opening view of his empty right hand, planted foot and phone together. Background: Dark-green three-wheeler bodywork and part of its rear wheel remain at frame left. A strip of the green-painted shop wall occupies the upper-left background; wet concrete, the kerb and open drainage fill the lower and right portions. Kasun's red mannequin stands center-left with his visible lower chest and hips oriented screen right, both feet planted beside the kerb. His right hand hangs empty beside his right thigh, and his left hand rests empty beside the opposite hip. The orange phone lies clearly visible on the wet asphalt beside his right foot, close to the rear wheel at frame left and short of the open drain.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Standing eye height, slightly ahead of Kasun but still on the roadward side of the axis; 35mm medium torso framing in three-quarter profile. His direction reads across the image toward screen right, not toward the lens. Background: The green-painted wall and a small portion of the blue awning remain behind him on frame left, now softer and farther away. A grey shop shutter and weathered beige frontage occupy the center-right background. Kasun's red mannequin occupies center-left in a forward-leaning running pose, chest angled three-quarter toward screen right and head turned along the same rightward path. His right elbow is bent with the orange phone held securely at the lower-right edge of his torso, while his empty left hand is raised in the opposing running position. Leave space toward screen right, keeping his head in three-quarter profile rather than square to the camera.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Standing eye height on the roadward side, squared across the walking line; 50mm medium two-shot. Kasun occupies frame left and Anudi frame right, with a clear gap between them. Background: The same green-painted wall remains in the far-left background as a connection to the bay. The grey shutter sits behind the gap between the figures, with the weathered beige frontage behind Anudi at frame right. Anudi's blue mannequin stands at frame right beneath the umbrella, chest and head still facing screen right in profile. Her left hand holds the umbrella shaft, and her empty right hand hangs beside the tan handbag on her right hip. Kasun's red mannequin enters from frame left in a rightward step, chest and head facing toward Anudi, with his right hand carrying the orange phone slightly forward at waist height and his empty left hand lowered beside him. Preserve a clear interval between the phone and Anudi's right hand; neither mannequin touches the other.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
